My name is Ishmael.

A few years back, I had almost no money and nothing keeping me on land. So I decided to travel by sea and see the ocean parts of the world.

This is how I deal with feeling low and keep myself steady. When I start feeling grim, when my mood turns as gray as a wet November day, when I catch myself staring at coffin shops or trailing behind every funeral I pass, and especially when I feel so low that only sheer willpower stops me from walking into the street and knocking hats off strangers' heads — that's when I know it's time to go to sea.

Going to sea is my way of coping instead of turning to something more drastic. Some people might end their troubles dramatically, like Cato falling on his sword. I simply get on a ship instead.

None of this is unusual. If people looked closely at themselves, they'd find that at some point, almost everyone feels the same pull toward the ocean that I do.

Whenever I find myself growing grim about the mouth; whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in my soul; whenever I find myself involuntarily pausing before coffin warehouses, and bringing up the rear of every funeral I meet; and especially whenever my hypos get such an upper hand of me, that it requires a strong moral principle to prevent me from deliberately stepping into the street, and methodically knocking people's hats off—then, I account it high time to get to sea as soon as I can.
